record.context_brief: Minimal nonlocal energy in a prescribed degree class
record.original_question: For 1 < p < ∞ and integer d, let mp,d be the infimum of the p-th W^{1/p,p} seminorm among maps f:S^1→S^1 of degree d. Is mp,d = |d| mp,1 for every d? Is the infimum defining mp,d achieved? If this linear formula fails, is there an explicit formula for lim_{d→∞} mp,d/d = inf_{d>0} mp,d/d?

evidence.quote: given 1 < p < ∞ and d ∈ Z set (5.13) mp,d := Inf {|f|p W1/p,p ; f ∈ W1/p,p(S1; S1), deg f = d}.

Open Problem 5.4 ([BM, Open Problems 22 and 23]). Let 1 < p < ∞. Is true that (5.15) mp,d = |d|mp,1 ∀d ∈ Z? Is the inf in (5.13) achieved? The answer to both questions is positive for p = 2. Assuming that (5.15) does not hold, is there an explicit formula for (5.16) lim d→+∞ mp,d/d = inf d>0 mp,d/d?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $1<p<\infty$ and let $d\in\mathbb{Z}$. For maps $f\in W^{1/p,p}(\mathbb{S}^1;\mathbb{S}^1)$ (i.e. measurable maps from the unit circle to itself in the fractional Sobolev space of order $1/p$ and integrability $p$), the topological degree $\deg f\in\mathbb{Z}$ is well-defined. The Gagliardo seminorm is
$$|f|_{W^{1/p,p}}^p := \int_{\mathbb{S}^1}\int_{\mathbb{S}^1} \frac{|f(x)-f(y)|^p}{|x-y|^2}\,dx\,dy.$$
Define
$$m_{p,d} := \inf\bigl\{\,|f|_{W^{1/p,p}}^p \;:\; f\in W^{1/p,p}(\mathbb{S}^1;\mathbb{S}^1),\ \deg f = d\,\bigr\}.$$

(a) Is it true that $m_{p,d} = |d|\,m_{p,1}$ for every $d\in\mathbb{Z}$ and every $1<p<\infty$?

(b) Is the infimum defining $m_{p,d}$ attained?

(c) If the equality in (a) fails, is there an explicit formula for
$$\lim_{d\to+\infty}\frac{m_{p,d}}{d} = \inf_{d>0}\frac{m_{p,d}}{d}?$$

(It is known that the answers to (a) and (b) are affirmative when $p=2$.)
artifact.category_tag: fractional Sobolev maps to the circle
artifact.status_search_result: A recent preprint (2025) establishes existence of degree-one minimizers in $W^{1/p,p}(\mathbb{S}^1,\mathbb{S}^1)$ for $p\in[p',2]$ with $p'\approx 1.13924$, providing a partial affirmative answer to the attainment question (b) in a restricted range of $p$. The linear identity $m_{p,d}=|d|m_{p,1}$ for all $d$ and the explicit limit formula in (c) appear to remain open in general; only the case $p=2$ is fully settled.

status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on attainment of the infimum defining m_{p,1} for a range of p around 2.
